observations: Native manual-window frame durations remain below 33.333 ms for all 600 recorded frames; these are browser rendering frames, not GPU execution or display presentation measurements.

The initial activation includes an approximately 1.332-second native frame, with approximately 1.28 seconds attributed to script in the inspector. This cold-start cost is separate from the settled interaction window.

The pinned renderer emits a THREE.Clock deprecation warning per mount. A later extended textured reopen run also reaches Safari context-quota warnings and INVALID_OPERATION: loseContext: context already lost. Lost/detached counters alone do not prove native context capacity is reclaimed.
Graphics context loss and stable live counts do not establish a phone CPU/OS/GPU memory trend.
pending: Real live reduced-motion check and slow loading/cancellation
Native retained-memory and context-quota investigation, including instrumentation overhead

afterStop.note: The one-second wait did not exclude all damping; the longer post-stop sequence confirms eventual idle.

bitmapLifetimeAfterRepeat.method: Test-only wrapper around native createImageBitmap and each returned bitmap.close, installed before activation. Counters retain no bitmap objects or model data.

nativeMemory.method: Native Safari Memory timeline with Collect garbage requested through Inspector before and after another ten reopens; model closed at both ends. Memory instrumentation configured without screenshots. Raw export remains ignored and owner-readable.
nativeMemory.result: Inconclusive native-memory trend: JavaScript category decreases, but Page and total categories increase. Do not claim the phone memory acceptance check passed; distinguish allocator/browser capacity from retained application objects with a longer plateau/allocation study.
nativeMemory.contextQuotaWarnings: During the second textured reopen batch, Safari reports too many active WebGL contexts and already-lost context errors despite previous contexts being recorded as lost/detached. Cause not isolated; no native-memory pass.

realVisibilityChecks.note: Multiple real hidden/visible events observed; one boundary records one additional submitted frame. This is separate from simulated browser coverage.

subjectiveFeedback.question: Did any of the three models stutter? Is the iPhone charging, is Low Power Mode on or off, and does it feel noticeably warm?
subjectiveFeedback.interpretation: Initial feedback reports no perceived stuttering. Superseded for overall visual correctness by the later landscape clipping and flicker report. Charging, Low Power Mode and thermal state were not separately confirmed.

reportedRegressions.userReport: in sideway full screen the model isn't centred. also, after I move it for a while and stop, the model starts flickering fir a few minutes and then stops flickering
reportedRegressions.screenshot: IMG_0622.PNG supplied by user; textured model visibly clipped at the lower edge of the landscape stage
reportedRegressions.expandedMode: Dialog fallback; device events show fullscreen false, dialog true
reportedRegressions.response: Bind the Canvas wrapper to the actual clamped stage using absolute positioning; keep DPR stable during orbit instead of changing it between motion and rest. User confirms the subsequent physical iPhone retest works.

physicalRetest.requestedChecks: Textured model in landscape expanded preview; move the model and stop, checking centering and whether flicker returns.
physicalRetest.result: User-confirmed visual pass for the two reported defects.
physicalRetest.build: Fresh isolated production session with the absolute Canvas layout, top-aligned expanded dialog and stable DPR.
physicalRetest.limits: Subjective confirmation only; no new frame, memory, thermal or timing measurements were supplied. Does not resolve the earlier extended-session memory/context-quota observations.
